title: k8s-node-provisioning-debug-notes
content:
Context:
- Spinning up a new node pool for low-priority batch jobs (spot/ephemeral). Seeing intermittent failures where nodes join the cluster but kubelet goes NotReady after ~5-10 minutes.
- Affects batch-worker pool in us-west-2, autoscaling enabled via cluster-autoscaler + cloud-provider.
- First noticed 2025-10-29 after we pushed a CRD update + Helm chart bump for node-init container.

Symptoms observed:
- Node initially Ready for a few minutes, then transitions to NotReady.
- kubelet logs show docker/containerd image pull issues sometimes, and other times show taints applied then failing liveness probes for node-problem-detector.
- Some nodes never register kube-proxy properly (iptables rules missing).
- Intermittent errors in cloud-provider auth: "metadata API rate limited" and occasional 403 from metadata for instance identity.

Commands I ran (raw outputs trimmed/pasted):
1) Check node status quickly after repro:
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep batch-worker
batch-worker-6f9k   NotReady   1d   ...   10.0.3.45   ip-10-0-3-45.us-west-2.compute.internal

2) Describe failing node:
$ kubectl describe node ip-10-0-3-45.us-west-2.compute.internal
(snip)
Conditions:
  Type             Status  LastHeartbeatTime                 Reason   Message
  Ready            False   2026-02-11T17:23:16Z            KubeletNotReady   Kubelet stopped posting node status

Events:
  17:22:50   Warning   FailedScheduling   pod "batch-job-..."   0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
  17:23:20   Warning   NodeNotReady       Node ip-10-0-3-45 became NotReady

3) kubelet journal: (ssh into node via bastion)
$ sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
Feb 11 17:22:58 ip-10-0-3-45 kubelet[1423]: E0211 17:22:58.123456   1423 kubelet.go:2264] Failed to update node status: Post "https://api.internal.k8s:6443/api/v1/nodes/ip-10-0-3-45/status": context deadline exceeded
Feb 11 17:23:01 ip-10-0-3-45 kubelet[1423]: W0211 17:23:01.987654   1423 docker_shim.go:... Failed to remove container "kube-proxy": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = network plugin not ready

4) containerd status + CRI checks:
$ sudo crictl ps -a
CONTAINER           IMAGE               CREATED   STATE   NAME
... kube-proxy         k8s.gcr.io/kube-proxy:v1.26.1  Running
... node-problem-detector  redwood/node-problem-detector:latest Exited (1)

5) node-init helm values we rolled out (relevant snippet):
nodeInit:
  enabled: true
  image: "registry.redwood.company/node-init:2026-01-28"
  initScripts:
    - path: /opt/init/attach-ebs.sh
      timeoutSeconds: 120
  postJoinHook: |
    # small script to start node-problem-detector
    systemctl start node-problem-detector || true

Hypotheses so far:
- Node-init image might be incompatible with new AMI kernel (we rolled AMI 2026-01-25). If init fails, some systemd units don't start (node-problem-detector, kube-proxy).
- Cloud metadata API throttling (we've increased pool scale recently) causes kubelet to fail identity calls, which leads to status update failures and kube-proxy / CNI not configuring.
- Systemd dependency order: postJoinHook runs before some network interfaces are up, causing race conditions for iptables/CNI setup.
- A recent Helm chart change added a taint to batch-worker nodes (we wanted to isolate), but tolerations not set in some pods -> scheduling pressure and weird states.

Things I tried (and results):
- Reverted node-init image to previous tag (2025-12-10) on a test pool: nodes are stable for 24h so far. Strong signal that node-init image is culprit.
- Added retry/backoff in postJoinHook for starting node-problem-detector; still saw occasional NotReady after 2-4 hours.
- Increased metadata API client retry in cloud-provider config (from 3 -> 8 retries with exponential backoff): reduced frequency of "metadata rate limited" logs but not eliminated.
- Turned off taint rollout on one test pool to check scheduler behavior: pods scheduled normally, but some nodes still went NotReady (so taint wasn't sole cause).

Notes from pair debugging with Jordan:
- Jordan saw similar symptoms that correlated with a kernel update (dmesg showed xfs complaints on ephemeral device attach). We suspect node-init's attach-ebs.sh might be assuming /dev/nvme0n1 naming vs nvme1n1 on new AMI -> attach script fails and some mounts not created.
- We saw node IP change right before NotReady in cloud provider logs: instance reconfigured? Might be from ephemeral device attach causing a network reinit.

Quick repro checklist (manual):
- Create small ASG with AMI 2026-01-25 + node-init:2026-01-28 + same helm chart
- Watch cloud-init logs (/var/log/cloud-init-output.log) and /var/log/node-init.log
- Tail kubelet journal and api-server audit logs for status update failures

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Roll node-init image back in prod batch-worker pool if test reversion stays stable for 48h (owners: Emily/Jordan). Refer JIRA-INFRA-342 for approvals.
- [ ] Instrument attach-ebs.sh: add more verbose logging + safe device discovery (use nvme list/lsblk + wait loops). Add to PR-1287.
- [ ] Add guard in Helm values: postJoinHook should wait for network-online.target before starting node-problem-detector.
- [ ] Open a cloud-provider ticket with cloud team to raise metadata API limits for scale-up spikes (Morgan to own).
- [ ] Add kubelet status update retries + longer timeouts in cluster config as temporary mitigation.
- [ ] Add alert that tracks node NotReady count within 30m after scale-up events (to detect regression earlier).

Random notes / scratch ideas:
- Could we swap attach-ebs.sh to use volume-attachment API instead of relying on ephemeral device names? Might be safer.
- Consider switching node-init image to non-root user builds to avoid unexpected permissions issues causing systemd failures.

References / links:
- JIRA-INFRA-342 (main ticket)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/PR-1287 (node-init logging & fixes)

Last manual check: 2026-02-12 09:14PT - test pool with reverted image is green (12 nodes ready). Will monitor for 48h before wider rollback.

-- Emily
